candidates.title: First quantum photonic processor operated in orbit
candidates.summary: University of Vienna processor launched on Falcon 9 performed two-photon interference and programmable operations in LEO.

candidates.title: Google rolls out Gemini 4 Argon frontier model to cyber defenders first
candidates.summary: Released via the Fairwind Program without cyber guardrails; 77.9% on DeepSWE v1.1, 1M context; general availability later.

candidates.title: OpenAI unveils 'Dots' always-on personal AI agents
candidates.summary: Persistent GPT-6 Astra agents with their own cloud VM and browser, 4,000+ app plugins, shared memory across ChatGPT/Slack/Teams; Pro and Business Premium first.

candidates.title: Bats first evolved in Europe 65 million years ago
candidates.summary: Bat1K Nature study of 103 genomes plus 44 fossils places bat origins in late-Palaeocene Europe; flight and echolocation arose early.

candidates.title: Apple Pay launches in India with Axis Bank
candidates.summary: Live Sep 30 on iPhone/iPad/Watch for Axis Visa/Mastercard credit cards at Zomato, Blinkit, Croma and others; no UPI support at launch.

candidates.title: AMD to acquire Fei-Fei Li's World Labs for $8.2B
candidates.summary: All-stock deal brings spatial-intelligence/world-model startup into AMD; Fei-Fei Li to become AMD EVP and chief scientist.

candidates.title: Autonomous AI agent breaches cybersecurity nonprofit DIVD
candidates.summary: An AI agent exploited two Zammad zero-days, then ran AitM and password spraying; DIVD called it 'loud and very, very messy' and promised an Oct 1 update.

candidates.title: Apple sets iPhone Duo foldable pre-order dates
candidates.summary: Apple's $1,999 foldable iPhone Duo: 'Get Ready' from Oct 12, pre-orders Oct 16, availability Oct 23 in 70+ countries including India.

candidates.title: Record 10-minute X-ray flash may reveal birth of a magnetar
candidates.summary: Einstein Probe event EP250704a links minutes-long X-ray flashes to neutron-star mergers forming magnetars (Science Bulletin).

candidates.title: OpenAI says Moonshot AI-linked users ran distillation campaign against its reasoning
candidates.summary: OpenAI report: 16,000 requests in a day from 4,000+ users, 15,000-account cluster, aimed at extracting protected reasoning; attributed to people tied to Kimi maker Moonshot.

candidates.title: Redmi 17C 5G launches in India Oct 1
candidates.summary: Budget 5G phone with 6.9-inch 120Hz display, Dimensity 6300 and 6,000mAh battery; expected under Rs 20,000.

candidates.title: Black hole jets heat gas far beyond galaxies' visible edges
candidates.summary: DESI + LOFAR study finds jets leave glowing hydrogen trails hundreds of thousands of light-years long, possibly halting star formation.

candidates.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.1 Sol at DevDay 2026
candidates.summary: Upgrade to GPT-6 Sol, positioned near GPT-6 Astra capability at one-fifth the price ($2/M input, $10/M output); system card published.

candidates.title: Qualcomm to acquire PickNik, steward of MoveIt robotics framework
candidates.summary: Qualcomm announced at ROSCon Toronto it will buy PickNik to push open robotics and physical AI; MoveIt stays open source (date approximate, late Sept).

candidates.summary: Roundups list Vivo V80, Vivo S2 FE, Oppo F35 series, Oppo K15 Pro, OnePlus 16, Motorola Edge 70 Neo and more for October.

candidates.title: India's October smartphone launches: Redmi 17C 5G, Vivo V80, Oppo F35, Moto Edge 70 Neo
candidates.summary: October 2026 India launch lineup; OnePlus 16 is expected in China in October and in India in November.

candidates.title: Tesla Optimus leans on Chinese suppliers; hands still a bottleneck
candidates.summary: Tesla inspects Chinese suppliers for Optimus ramp; reports say hands with 100+ parts are still hand-assembled.

candidates.title: Qualcomm confirms it is evaluating Samsung's 2nm process
candidates.summary: Qualcomm exec calls Samsung its 'strongest partner'; no product is committed to Samsung foundry yet.

candidates.title: Earth's inner core may change day length by milliseconds
candidates.summary: Model: a gravitational tug between the misshapen inner core and mantle swings the core ~2.35 degrees over a 60-70 year cycle.

candidates.title: OpenAI seeks $30B funding at ~$1.4 trillion valuation
candidates.summary: Bloomberg-reported early-stage talks for a pre-IPO bridge round; run-rate revenue above $40B; IPO pushed to 2027.

candidates.title: Citrix NetScaler zero-days (CVE-2026-88771/88772) exploited globally
candidates.summary: Two CVSS 9.5 unauthenticated RCE flaws, exploited since early September and added to CISA KEV; Mandiant/GTIG report WHIPSHOT/SLAPSHOT implants.

candidates.title: Geely buys 30% of Nio's battery-swapping unit
candidates.summary: Deal values Nio Power at ~$2.4B; Nio takes 10% of Geely's Haohan Energy and the two will unify swapping standards.

candidates.title: The Moon drifts 3.8 cm farther away every year
candidates.summary: Lunar laser ranging off the Apollo retroreflectors (the first was placed in July 1969) shows the Moon receding about 3.8 cm/year (3.83 cm). Tides slowing Earth's spin drive the drift.

candidates.title: Dinosaur days were only 23.5 hours long
candidates.summary: Daily growth rings in a 70-million-year-old rudist clam show the Late Cretaceous year had 372 days and a day lasted about 23.5 hours (AGU Paleoceanography, 2020).

candidates.title: Your nose may tell apart over 1 trillion smells
candidates.summary: A 2014 Rockefeller study in Science estimated humans can distinguish more than 1 trillion odor mixtures, against the old figure of 10,000. ASU researchers dispute the math, so call it an estimate.

candidates.title: ESA-China SMILE mission begins science, releases first images
candidates.summary: SMILE's UV imager captured the full northern auroral oval, first such view in ~18 years, as science operations start.

candidates.title: Sugar amplifies antibiotic damage to gut microbiome
candidates.summary: Nature study of 9,400+ meals: each 100 g of sweets cut gut diversity 24% during antibiotics in stem-cell transplant patients; Enterococcus overgrowth.

candidates.title: DarkSide rules out range of 'nuclear' composite dark matter
candidates.summary: Seven-year DarkSide-50 search found no composite ultraheavy dark matter, constraining its properties (Physical Review D).

candidates.title: OpenAI introduces ChatGPT Space shared team workspace and meeting note-taker
candidates.summary: Persistent workspace where teams, ChatGPT and Dots collaborate, mixing Slack/Notion/Drive-style tools with embedded agents.

candidates.title: Meta has its best month since 2022 on AI momentum
candidates.summary: META closed Sep 30 at $725.18, up ~27% in September, driven by the Muse agent's success.

candidates.title: Gotion claims solid-state battery breakthrough: 400 Wh/kg target
candidates.summary: VW-backed Gotion targets 400 Wh/kg and ~$150/kWh for all-solid-state cells, says cells passed abuse tests with no smoke or fire.

candidates.title: Humanoid robot shipments surge 432% in H1 2026
candidates.summary: Nearly 25,000 humanoids shipped in H1; AgiBot overtakes Unitree; IDC lifts 2030 forecast to 750,000+ units.

candidates.title: Marine heatwaves hide 150% more heat exposure
candidates.summary: VIMS study of 2,580 heatwaves in 20 US estuaries finds warming before/after heatwaves more than doubles cumulative heat stress.

candidates.title: OpenSSL patches 14 flaws including high-severity DTLS memory leak
candidates.summary: CVE-2026-84782 can leak heap memory in plaintext or crash DTLS apps; fixed in 4.0.3, 3.6.5, 3.5.9, 3.4.8; no known exploitation.

candidates.title: Sunlight is 8 minutes old, but its energy is up to 170,000 years old
candidates.summary: Light crosses from the Sun to Earth in about 8 min 20 s, but the energy takes roughly 10,000-170,000 years to random-walk out from the core (NASA cites ~170,000 years). Neutrinos make the same trip in about 2 seconds.

candidates.title: Honey from Egyptian tombs is still edible
candidates.summary: Archaeologists found honey in Egyptian tombs more than 3,000 years old that had not spoiled. Honey resists spoiling because of its low water content, a pH of about 3-4.5, and hydrogen peroxide made by the enzyme glucose oxidase.

candidates.title: Jupiter's Great Red Spot is shrinking but still wider than Earth
candidates.summary: The Great Red Spot measured about 41,000 km across in the late 1800s and 23,300 km at Voyager in 1979. Hubble now measures it at about 16,500 km (10,250 miles), still wider than Earth.

candidates.title: Apollo footprints are still on the Moon
candidates.summary: With no wind or rain, Apollo bootprints and rover tracks are still there. NASA's LRO photographed them at all six landing sites at about 25-50 cm per pixel, and they could last millions of years unless micrometeorites disturb them.

candidates.title: Greenland sharks live for centuries
candidates.summary: Radiocarbon dating of eye lenses (Science, 2016) put the largest shark (502 cm) at 392 +/-120 years, with a lifespan of at least 272 years and sexual maturity at about 156 years. It is the longest-lived vertebrate known.

candidates.title: The 'immortal' jellyfish ages in reverse
candidates.summary: When damaged or starving, Turritopsis dohrnii turns back into a juvenile polyp within about 24-72 hours through transdifferentiation. Lab colonies have restarted their life cycle up to 10 times in 2 years.

candidates.title: Voyager 1 is about to be one light-day from Earth
candidates.summary: Voyager 1 is due to reach 1 light-day from Earth (about 25.9 billion km, 16.1 billion mi, 173 AU) on Nov 18, 2026. A signal will then take 24 hours each way.

candidates.title: Altman: no OpenAI IPO until it can make confident safety claims
candidates.summary: Sam Altman told reporters OpenAI must be able to make confident safety claims about AI 'going rogue' before going public.

candidates.title: Google's Fairwind cyber-defender program passes 650 organizations
candidates.summary: Fairwind opened Sept 3 with Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber; Wiz used Argon to find a critical healthcare-software bug that earlier models missed.

candidates.title: Meta launches Meta Enterprise Platform and Muse for Small Business
candidates.summary: Meta hires MongoDB CEO CJ Desai to lead its new enterprise unit and launches Muse agents for small businesses.

candidates.title: Is the internet ready for AI agents like Meta Muse?
candidates.summary: NPR/CNN look at the risks of autonomous agents as Muse passes 2.5M downloads and rivals follow.

candidates.title: Apple Invites app update adds full-res shared albums and photoreal Image Playground backgrounds
candidates.summary: Small Apple app update with AI-generated photoreal backgrounds.

candidates.title: Nvidia launches Open Agent Safety Platform to rein in rogue AI agents
candidates.summary: Jensen Huang introduced software and hardware security layers around AI agents (Sep 28, just before the window).

candidates.title: Anthropic's self-set provable-inference deadline passes without word
candidates.summary: The Sep 30 RSP 'Phase 1' milestone for signing model outputs passed with no public update, per Forkast and Yahoo Finance commentary.

candidates.title: California AI rules take effect Oct 1
candidates.summary: Whistleblower protections at frontier AI developers, automated employment-decision rules and synthetic-content transparency duties begin.

candidates.title: Arivihan raises $10M Series A for AI learning platform
candidates.summary: Accel and Prosus co-led the round for the IIT Roorkee-founded AI study-plan and doubt-solving app.

candidates.title: IndiaAI Mission backs 20 indigenous sovereign AI models
candidates.summary: 12 LLMs and 8 SLMs, including Sarvam, Gnani.AI and BharatGen; 93 lakh GPU hours sanctioned (status as of Sep 28).

candidates.title: Professional service robot sales up 24%; humanoids emerge as a segment
candidates.summary: About 250,000 units shipped in 2025, including ~7,000 full-size humanoids; commercialization hurdles remain.

candidates.title: Curiosity rover marks 5,000 sols on Mars with 'postcard'
candidates.summary: NASA blended morning and afternoon navcam panoramas from Mount Sharp to mark 5,000 Martian days.

candidates.title: A blue whale's heart can beat just twice a minute
candidates.summary: In the first ECG recording of a blue whale (Stanford, PNAS 2019), its heart rate fell to as low as 2 bpm on dives and peaked at 37 bpm at the surface. NOAA puts the heart at about 400 lb, the weight of a studio piano.

candidates.title: Wombats poop cubes
candidates.summary: Wombats are the only known animals that make cube-shaped scat. Their intestine has alternating stiff and flexible regions (stiff zones about 2x thicker and 4x stiffer) that shape the feces. The work won a 2019 Ig Nobel and was published in Soft Matter in 2021.

candidates.title: Your eye can detect a single photon
candidates.summary: A 2016 Nature Communications study (Rockefeller University and IMP Vienna, more than 30,000 trials) found people detected single photons 51.6% of the time, above chance, and were right 60% of the time when confident.

candidates.title: The world's largest desert is Antarctica
candidates.summary: Antarctica (about 14.2 million km2 / 5.5 million mi2) is the largest desert, nearly twice the Sahara. Its interior gets only about 5 cm of precipitation a year, and the desert threshold is 25 cm.

candidates.title: Glass frogs turn invisible by hiding their blood in their liver
candidates.summary: Sleeping northern glassfrogs pull nearly 90% of their red blood cells out of circulation and pack them into the liver without clotting. Their skin and muscle then let through over 90% of visible light (Science, Dec 2022, Duke/AMNH).

candidates.title: Artemis Accords reach 76 signatories
candidates.summary: Albania, Croatia, Cote d'Ivoire and San Marino join; principals meet in Antalya alongside IAC from Oct 5.

candidates.title: Olympus Mons is nearly 3 times taller than Everest
candidates.summary: Mars' Olympus Mons rises about 26 km above the surrounding plains, roughly three times Everest's height, and is about 585 km wide (wider than Arizona), yet its slopes are only 2-5 degrees.

candidates.title: Saturn would float in a big enough bathtub
candidates.summary: Saturn's average density is about 0.687 g/cm3, below water's ~1 g/cm3, which makes it the only planet less dense than water (it couldn't really float, since its gravity would pull the water in).

candidates.title: Bananas are slightly radioactive
candidates.summary: Bananas contain potassium-40 (about 0.0117% of natural potassium). One banana gives about 15 Bq and a dose of about 0.1 microsieverts, the informal 'banana equivalent dose'. The body excretes excess potassium, so eating more doesn't raise your dose.

candidates.title: Challenger Deep pressure is over 1,000 atmospheres
candidates.summary: Challenger Deep is about 10,935 m deep (+/-6 m, from a 2021 Deep-Sea Research I study). Pressure there is about 1,086 bar, roughly 1,071 times sea-level pressure or about 8 tons per square inch, and the water is 1-4 C.

candidates.title: Pando: a 'forest' that is one single organism
candidates.summary: Utah's Pando aspen is about 47,000 genetically identical stems on one root system across about 43 hectares (106 acres). It weighs roughly 6,000 metric tons, and a recent estimate puts its age at 12,000-37,000 years.

candidates.title: You are made of about 7 octillion atoms
candidates.summary: A 70 kg human has about 7x10^27 atoms. About 62-63% of them are hydrogen, ~24% oxygen and ~12% carbon by count, but oxygen is ~61% of body mass.

candidates.title: Earth's inner core is as hot as the Sun's surface, yet solid
candidates.summary: The inner core is about 5,400 C (~5,700 K, 9,800 F), about the temperature of the Sun's surface. Immense pressure keeps it solid.

candidates.title: The mantis shrimp punches like a bullet
candidates.summary: A mantis shrimp's club strikes at about 23 m/s (83 km/h) with acceleration around 10,400 g, similar to a .22 bullet. The cavitation bubbles it creates collapse with a second impact and a brief flash of heat.

candidates.title: Half your oxygen comes from the ocean
candidates.summary: According to NOAA, the ocean produces roughly 50% of Earth's oxygen, mostly from phytoplankton. One tiny cyanobacterium, Prochlorococcus (about 0.6 um), alone may make 5-10%+ of the oxygen we breathe.

candidates.title: A hummingbird's heart beats 1,200 times a minute
candidates.summary: An active hummingbird's heart beats up to about 1,200 bpm (250-500 at rest). In nightly torpor it can drop to about 50 bpm.

candidates.title: The Sun holds 99.8% of the solar system's mass
candidates.summary: The Sun holds 99.8% of all mass in the solar system. All the planets, moons, asteroids and comets together make up only about 0.2%.

candidates.title: Gallium: the metal that melts in your hand
candidates.summary: Gallium melts at 29.76 C, below body temperature (37 C), yet boils only at about 4,000 F (~2,400 C). Like water, it expands when it freezes.

candidates.title: It rains diamonds inside Neptune and Uranus
candidates.summary: SLAC X-ray laser experiments (2017, 2022) shock-compressed plastic to ice-giant conditions. The carbon turned into nanodiamonds within 50-femtosecond snapshots, which supports 'diamond rain' deep inside Neptune and Uranus.

candidates.title: Everest isn't the closest point to space: Chimborazo is
candidates.summary: Earth's equatorial bulge makes Ecuador's Chimborazo, just 1 degree south of the equator, the summit farthest from Earth's center. It is over 2 km (about 2,072 m) farther out than Everest's 8,848 m peak.

candidates.title: 240-million-year-old Tanzanian fossil shifts dinosaur timeline
candidates.summary: New dicynodont Dinodontosaurus isiyavamanda links Tanzania and South America, suggesting 'oldest dinosaur' beds are younger.

candidates.title: Your stomach lining replaces itself every few days
candidates.summary: The stomach's surface lining is renewed about every 3-5 days (some sources say 2-4) to survive acid with a pH of about 1.5-3.5.

candidates.title: Water can boil and freeze at the same time
candidates.summary: At the triple point, 0.01 C (273.16 K) and 611.657 Pa, ice, liquid water and vapor coexist in equilibrium. It has served as a reference point for calibrating thermometers.

candidates.title: Cows have best friends
candidates.summary: A 2011 University of Northampton study found cows penned with a preferred partner had lower heart rates and cortisol than with a non-preferred herd-mate.

candidates.title: Microsoft revamps Copilot with Home, Code and Autopilot agent
candidates.summary: Redesigned Copilot adds a persistent Autopilot agent, app generation, and Copilot Managed Runtime hosting inside the M365 boundary (announced Sep 25, slightly before the window).
